The *Daṇḍadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 357) is a biographical poem situated within the Therāpadāna collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The title indicates a narrative centering on the karmic fruition of an elder’s past gift of a staff or stick (*daṇḍa*) to an enlightened being, following the standard thematic convention of the Apadāna literature [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral identifies no ancient translation parallels in other canonical languages but records five modern translations in five languages for the text [SuttaCentral].

No cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan meet the alignment threshold in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus reveals substantial Pali-internal text reuse, showing 40 matches across 18 canonical and post-canonical works [DharmaNexus]. The closest parallel occurs with another homonymous poem in the collection, the second *Daṇḍadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 528), which shares a large opening section (§§0.2–3.4 with 0.9 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. The poem also shares significant material (§§0.3–3.3) with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Paṭhamo bhāgo) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, formulaic closing sequences occurring across segments 3.1–6.1 are widely shared with other Therāpadāna accounts of gift-giving, including the *Vāsidāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 242), *Mañcadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 360), *Āluvadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 280), and *Pattadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 248) [DharmaNexus].
